Sanofi's Earnings Upgrade Meets a Pipeline Reckoning as Analysts Split on the Road Ahead
sum: Two brokerage houses moved on Sanofi within days of each other, and the pair of notes frame the same central question: how much of the French drugmaker's near-term earnings power is durable, and what replaces it once the Dupixent price tailwind fades.

Citi lifted its 2026–2030 earnings forecasts by 5–10% depending on the year, pointing to fatter margins and a more favourable net price for Dupixent. The bank credits sharper discount management and the US 340B programme for the improvement, and expects that pricing support to hold through 2026 and 2027. Growth estimates beyond that window were left untouched. Citi raised its price target to EUR 93 from EUR 78 while keeping a Neutral rating — a higher valuation paired with a still-cautious recommendation.

The upgrade cycle began earlier in the week. BNP Paribas Exane moved Sanofi from Neutral to Outperform on Monday, with media reports putting the new target at EUR 102, up from EUR 79. That re-rating was cited as a driver of the share price gain that day, set against the positive backdrop of quarterly growth and a raised full-year outlook.

The numbers behind the optimism came from the third quarter of 2026, when Sanofi posted currency-adjusted revenue growth of 14.3%. Dupixent was the principal engine, with sales climbing 34.8% to EUR 5.7 billion. Adjusted earnings per share reached EUR 3.55, a 19.6% increase at constant exchange rates.
Management used the quarter to raise its 2026 guidance: revenue growth in the low teens percentage range and adjusted EPS growth in the mid-teens, both at constant currencies.

Citi's caution on the out-years rests partly on rival programmes closing in. The bank expects AstraZeneca's Tozorakimab to win approval in COPD during the first quarter of 2027. Pfizer's Tilrekimig and AbbVie/Apogee's Zumilokibart are both in Phase III, with launches anticipated in 2029 or 2030. Those dates turn competition into a concrete checkpoint for Sanofi's outlook — pressure could build if the rival programmes hit their expected approvals and market entries. On the flip side, Citi flags broader drug uptake, pipeline progress and partnership deals as potential positive catalysts.

sum: Sanofi повысила свои прогнозы на весь год после третьего квартала, в котором продажи с поправкой на валютные курсы выросли на 14,3%, а выручка достигла 14,44 млрд евро. Скорректированная прибыль на акцию за период составила 3,55 евро. Французский производитель лекарств в настоящее время прогнозирует невысокий рост выручки, выражающийся двузначными числами, при постоянных обменных курсах на 2026 год, а также процентное увеличение скорректированной прибыли на акцию на той же валютно-нейтральной основе.

Обновление, объявленное 30 октября, вызвало быструю реакцию аналитического сообщества. В понедельник BNP Paribas Exane перевел акции Sanofi с «нейтрального» на «лучше рынка», подняв целевую цену с 79 евро до 102 евро. Брокер указал на то, что третий квартал превзойдет ожидания благодаря силе Dupixent. UBS в тот день также повысил свою цель с 78 евро до 88 евро, хотя и сохранил нейтральный рейтинг, при этом в репортажах отмечалось сохраняющееся беспокойство инвесторов по поводу роста после того, как вклад Dupixent исчезнет.
Кроме того, сегодня Sanofi опубликовала данные об общей доле и правах голоса за октябрь 2026 года.

Что касается разработки, Sanofi 28 октября подтвердила, что пятый пациент получил дозу в рамках третьего этапа европейского исследования комбинированной вакцины против гриппа и Covid-19. По соглашению с Novavax этот этап регистрации привел к выплате американскому специалисту по вакцинам промежуточной выплаты в размере 125 миллионов долларов. Еще 75 миллионов долларов причитаются Novavax после завершения передачи производственных технологий — это отдельное условие от уже разблокированного платежа за прогресс в испытаниях.

По сообщениям СМИ, Санофи и Университет науки и технологий Халифы подписали соглашение о стратегических исследованиях 4 ноября. Партнеры будут изучать генетические связи с астмой и хронической обструктивной болезнью легких (ХОБЛ) в Объединенных Арабских Эмиратах. Одобрение комитета по этике и разрешение регулирующих органов в Абу-Даби уже получены для исследования, которое фокусируется на геномных связях с двумя респираторными заболеваниями. В ходе сотрудничества не было объявлено о какой-либо новой терапии.

Агентство Reuters сообщило вчера, что Управление по санитарному надзору за качеством пищевых продуктов и медикаментов США приостановило свою программу ускоренной проверки лекарств, основанную на ваучерах.

sum: Sanofi (ENXTPA:SAN) pushed its influenza COVID 19 combination vaccine into Phase 3 testing in Europe, a high profile respiratory vaccine project that triggered sizeable milestone payouts to partner Novavax.

For anyone tracking Sanofi shares, that single step does two things at once. It moves a late stage pipeline asset closer to potential commercialization, and it highlights how partnered vaccine platforms could affect future economics for both sides.

Sanofi shares have picked up momentum recently, with a 20.96% 1 month share price return and a 13.32% 3 month share price return helping lift the stock to €86.61. The 1 year total shareholder return of 1.47% and 5 year total shareholder return of 18.45% point to a steadier long run journey that sets current excitement around the flu COVID combo and the firm’s raised 2026 guidance alongside a more measured performance record.
Surf 568 high quality undiscovered gems that, like Sanofi’s flu COVID combo effort, are quietly building late stage pipelines and partnerships that could reshape their future economics.

Bulls point to Sanofi’s respiratory pipeline and raised 2026 guidance. Bears focus on mixed nine month earnings. Which story shows up more clearly once you line that up against today’s valuation metrics?

On the valuation side, the narrative fair value for Sanofi sits at €72.23 versus the recent €86.61 close. This highlights how much optimism is already in the price according to Szock, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who set out a detailed view on the stock.

Novavax Stock Slips as B. Riley Trims Target but Keeps Buy Rating
sum: Novavax finds itself caught between two narratives. On one side sits a beefed-up balance sheet and a fresh milestone check from Sanofi; on the other, a shrinking top line and a quarterly loss that refuses to budge. B. Riley Securities weighed both on Friday and came down cautiously optimistic, cutting its price target to $16 from $18 while leaving its buy rating in place.

The stock was down 2.9% on the day, a modest pullback that mirrors the analyst's own measured stance. The shares had already taken a harder knock earlier in the week, sliding 6.5% in the session following the earnings release.

Novavax closed the third quarter of 2026 with $627 million in cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities and restricted cash as of September 30. That is a substantial war chest by any measure. Yet the same quarterly filing, submitted Thursday, showed a net loss of $31 million — a reminder that the company is still burning through its reserves rather than adding to them.

Revenue for the quarter came in at $68 million, down 3% year over year. The combination of a declining top line and a negative bottom line is what makes the investment case genuinely difficult: investors must decide how much credit to give the financial safety net versus how much weight to place on the underlying business trajectory.

The revenue picture looks rather different when viewed across the full year. Roughly two weeks ago, Novavax raised its 2026 adjusted revenue guidance to a range of $385 million to $415 million. Embedded in that forecast is a $125 million milestone payment earned in October, triggered when Sanofi launched a Phase 3 trial in Europe for a combined influenza-COVID-19 vaccine.

That payment is a concrete building block of the annual outlook — and a double-edged one. It validates the partnership and provides real cash. But it also raises a question analysts will keep circling: how much of the guidance depends on this single event, and how much rests on the rest of the business?

For the more optimistic scenario to gain traction, Novavax needs to show that revenue is finding a floor. A steady top line, paired with a narrower loss, would give investors a business argument to set alongside the balance-sheet argument.

The split between a more bullish rating from Exane BNP Paribas and a cautious Hold stance from UBS gives investors two different readings of Sanofi's near-term risk and reward. The analyst revisions follow Sanofi's stronger third-quarter performance and higher 2026 outlook, which have kept Dupixent and the group's newer medicines at the center of the investment case. StockWatch: Nurix Nosedives as Sanofi Halts Phase I Immunology Candidate
sum: Nurix Therapeutics (Nasdaq: NRIX) suffered its worst one-day loss as a public company Wednesday when Sanofi (Euronext Paris: SAN and Nasdaq: SNY) terminated development of the Phase I immunology candidate SAR448272 (NX-3911)—a key program of the companies’ nearly seven-year, up to $ 2.5 billion collaboration to discover, develop, and commercialize protein degradation drugs for “challenging” diseases.

The rest of the collaboration continues despite Sanofi pulling the plug on SAR448272 (NX-3911), an oral signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) degrader that had been under study in a Phase I first-in-human trial in Europe (European Union Clinical Trials Register number 2026-526014-87-00). The trial began recruiting patients in Germany in July and had planned to expand recruitment into the Czech Republic, France, Italy, and Spain, a milestone that triggered a $10 million payment from Sanofi to Nurix in August.

STAT6, a key drug target in type 2 inflammation, is among the five targets identified by the companies in their collaboration, which took effect in January 2020 when Sanofi paid Nurix $55 million upfront. At the time, Sanofi committed to paying Nurix up to $2.5 billion in total payments, most of that tied to achieving research, preclinical, clinical, regulatory, and sales milestones.

As of August 31, Sanofi had paid Nurix a total $129 million—the $55 million upfront; $22 million in 2021 when Sanofi exercised an option to expand from three to five targets; $22 million for achieving research milestones; and $30 million for license extension fees—according to Nurix’s Form 10-Q quarterly report for the third quarter, filed October 13.

Nurix insisted that its recent cash runway guidance would not be affected by Sanofi’s halting development of SAR448272. Nurix said it had enough cash to fund operations into the second half of 2029 based on its $1.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of August 31.

“While [Tuesday]’s news is disappointing, Nurix remains in a strong position, with a substantial cash runway, three clinical-stage programs across our wholly owned and partnered portfolio, and an exciting preclinical pipeline,” Arthur T. Sands, MD, PhD, Nurix president and CEO, stated Tuesday after the close of markets.

Sanofi Signals Appetite for Bigger Deals as Analysts Lift Targets
sum: Sanofi is prepared to look beyond its customary deal size, with finance chief François Roger indicating on 30 October that the French drugmaker would weigh acquisitions above its usual $2–5 billion range. The push is aimed at securing access to late-stage medicines or products already on the market, according to media reports.

Management has framed business development and bolt-on M&A as part of its growth blueprint for the period after Dupixent, the blockbuster immunology drug that anchors the group's earnings. The comments signal a broad willingness to pursue larger transactions rather than any specific target.

That willingness rests on a solid operating base. Sanofi reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of €14.44 billion, up 14.3% at constant exchange rates. Dupixent alone contributed €5.7 billion in the period, while adjusted earnings per share came in at €3.55, a constant-currency gain of 19.6%.

The beat on quarterly sales, powered by Dupixent, prompted RBC Capital to raise its price target on Sanofi from €75 to €80 on Monday while keeping a "Sector Perform" rating, per media reports. The broker paired its more generous valuation with caution about the group's development pipeline.

Those concerns have some grounding. Sanofi has halted development of SAR448272, an experimental STAT6 degrader licensed from Nurix, after new non-clinical findings failed to justify continuing in eczema, the company told Leerink Partners. Nurix expects no further milestone payments or royalties from the programme.

On the vaccine front, a European phase 3 trial of a combined influenza and COVID-19 shot has begun, triggering a $125 million milestone payment to partner Novavax. Novavax said Sanofi intends to launch a US phase 3 study in 2027 as well.

Roughly a week before the quarterly update, Sanofi lifted its full-year outlook. For 2026 it now projects constant-currency revenue growth in the low double-digit percentage range and an increase in adjusted EPS in the mid-teens percentage range.

Sanofi Draws Fresh Analyst Targets as Dupixent Powers Upgraded Outlook
sum: Two brokerage houses have nudged their price targets for Sanofi higher in the wake of the French drugmaker's stronger full-year guidance, though neither was moved to change its rating on the stock. Morgan Stanley lifted its objective from 82 to 86 euros on Tuesday, with analyst Thibault Boutherin keeping the shares at "Equal Weight." A day earlier, Barclays had raised its own target from 83 to 90 euros while also holding its "Equal Weight" stance, and a third research firm marked up its number without altering its recommendation either.

The round of revisions followed Sanofi's decision on 30 October to raise its forecast for 2026. Management now expects sales to grow at a low double-digit percentage rate at constant exchange rates, with adjusted earnings per share climbing by a mid-teens percentage on the same currency basis.

The upgraded guidance rests on a robust third quarter. Sanofi posted net sales of EUR 14,444 million for the period, a gain of 14.3 percent at constant exchange rates. Business earnings per share came in at EUR 3.55, up 19.6 percent on a currency-adjusted basis.
Dupixent remains the engine behind that performance. Revenue from the blockbuster drug jumped 34.8 percent to EUR 5.7 billion, underscoring its outsized role in the group's growth story.

Not every piece of news has been positive. Sanofi has halted development of SAR448272, an orally administered STAT6 degrader licensed from Nurix Therapeutics, after fresh non-clinical findings. According to media reports on Wednesday, the company told Leerink Partners that the results did not justify further work; the Phase 1 trial was stopped and the program shelved.

Nurix disclosed in a regulatory filing on Tuesday that it no longer anticipates future milestone payments or royalties tied to the candidate, so the termination also removes a projected revenue stream for the licensing partner. The decision reflects an assessment of that single molecule rather than a broader retreat from the STAT6 pathway, according to the reports.
On the business-development front, finance chief François Roger told Reuters on 30 October that Sanofi would consider acquisitions above its historical range of $2 billion to $5 billion.

Sanofi India stock: Q3 profit rises 54% as dividend declared
sum: Sanofi India reported a sharp rise in third-quarter profit and declared an interim dividend, according to CNBC TV18. The results relate to the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and were published on October 29, 2026.

Profit for the period rose 53.6 percent year on year to 117 crore INR from 76 crore INR. Revenue from operations increased 3.43 percent to 491.70 crore INR, while EBITDA grew 20.1 percent to 161 crore INR. The EBITDA margin widened to 32.8 percent from 28.2 percent.

Sanofi India said domestic net sales increased 2 percent and total net sales rose 4 percent from a year earlier. Its insulin portfolio grew 9 percent, with Lantus, Toujeo, Apidra and Soliqua contributing to performance.

The company said its diabetes injectable portfolio held a 55 percent market share. Its public-sector business expanded 85 percent, driven by new accounts in innovative analogue segments, while export sales recorded double-digit growth. Revenue from strategic partnerships in cardiovascular, oral anti-diabetes and central nervous system therapies remained broadly stable.
Sanofi India's board declared an interim dividend of 75 INR per equity share with a face value of 10 INR. November 5, 2026, was set as the record date for determining eligible shareholders.

Sanofi India is an India-based pharmaceutical business offering vaccines and therapies for diabetes, rare diseases and transplant needs, according to Sanofi India. The company is part of Sanofi, an R&D-driven biopharmaceutical group operating across medicines and vaccines in international markets.

Sanofi Stock And Why Earnings Guidance Raised Matters For Shareholders
sum: - Sanofi reported third quarter 2026 sales of €14,444 million and net income of €3,021 million, and raised full year 2026 earnings guidance while projecting low teens % sales growth and mid teens % business EPS growth at constant exchange rates.

- The firm is shaping its portfolio by discontinuing the SAR448272 oral STAT6 degrader program and advancing a Phase 3 influenza COVID 19 combination vaccine with Novavax's Nuvaxovid and high dose flu vaccine Efluelda or Fluzone in older adults.
- Attention now turns to how Sanofi's raised 2026 earnings outlook fits with the existing investment narrative around disciplined R&D governance.
Scan how Sanofi's guidance upgrade compares with peers by reviewing the hand picked 130 healthcare AI stocks that are also leaning on R&D intensive pipelines and vaccine platforms.

To own Sanofi, you need to believe disciplined R&D curation and a refocused vaccines and specialty portfolio can convert into steadier earnings, even with lumpier profit margins and one off items in the mix. The raised 2026 guidance points to management confidence in the operating plan, but it does not erase execution risk on later stage assets.

For the near term, the key catalyst is whether Sanofi can keep delivering on business EPS guidance while digesting portfolio clean ups such as the STAT6 degrader exit. The biggest current risk remains pipeline and vaccine execution, especially if competitive flu pricing or further program terminations weigh on margins and cash available for dividends.

The most relevant development for that catalyst is the Phase 3 influenza COVID 19 combination vaccine using Novavax's Nuvaxovid with Efluelda or Fluzone in adults over 60. This program sits directly in Sanofi's effort to refresh its vaccine mix toward higher value products after trimming its long term flu ambition and facing pricing pressure.

SLS Stock Snaps 4-Day Slide As Retail Eyes ASH Abstracts — Fresh Filings Reveal Bigger Swiss, Arizona Pension Bets
sum: - Investors are watching for possible SLS009 updates as Sellas expects Q4 topline results from its Phase 2 study in newly diagnosed AML.
- Sellas has a 600-square-foot booth at the Dec.12 to Dec.15 ASH meeting in New Orleans, in the same hall as several major drugmakers.
- Q3 holdings disclosures showed stake increases by Pictet, Swiss Life, Arizona State Retirement System and Xponance.

Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) snapped a four-day losing streak on Tuesday as retail investors looked ahead to abstracts from the American Society of Hematology (ASH), while fresh filings revealed increased holdings by Swiss asset managers and Arizona State Retirement System.

ASH will release regular meeting abstracts on Wednesday, with late-breaking abstracts following on Dec.7. Sellas investors are watching for possible updates on SLS009, or Tambiciclib, its CDK9 inhibitor being studied in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). In August, Sellas said it expected fourth-quarter topline results from its Phase 2 study of SLS009 in newly diagnosed AML.

The releases set the stage for the 68th ASH Annual Meeting and Exposition, running Dec.12 to Dec.15 in New Orleans. The event brings together blood-disease specialists, researchers and drugmakers, with more than 275 exhibitors expected. Sellas has a 600-square-foot booth at the far end of Hall G, directly beside the poster area. Its 20-by-30-foot space, Booth 138, puts it in the same hall as large exhibits from Eli Lilly, Takeda, Genentech and AstraZeneca.

Pfizer, Merck, Sanofi, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb have booths across other halls, while Johnson & Johnson is in Hall J, farther from Sellas. The broader exhibitor lineup includes GSK, Novartis, Amgen, Novo Nordisk, Daiichi Sankyo, Astellas, and Gilead and Kite Oncology.

sum: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals surged 13.33% to $927.89 on Friday, October 30, following third-quarter results that significantly beat estimates. Revenue rose 36% to $5.12 billion, and non-GAAP EPS jumped 70% to $20.07, driven by full Dupixent profit recognition from Sanofi and record sales across key drugs. The companies also expanded their alliance with a new $1 billion upfront deal. Technically, the stock exhibits strong bullish momentum with the RSI in overbought territory at 79. While a short-term pause is possible, a daily close above $930.46 targets $961.85, with key support at $870.49.

TradingKey - Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: REGN) jumped 13.33% to $927.89 on Friday, October 30, after third-quarter results beat estimates by a wide margin. It was the stock's highest close in at least a year, and it came on a day the S&P 500 fell 1.8%.

The key driver was Sanofi. Q3 was the first quarter Regeneron received its full share of Dupixent profits, after it finished repaying development costs that had been deducted from that share. The stock rose about 26% in October.

Revenue rose 36% to $5.12 billion, against about $4.58 billion expected, and non-GAAP EPS, which leaves out items such as stock-based pay, jumped 70% to $20.07, against an estimate of about $16.51, according to Trefis. GAAP EPS rose 35% to $18.45. CEO Leonard Schleifer called it "an outstanding quarter," with Dupixent, EYLEA HD and Libtayo each setting sales records.

Collaboration revenue from Sanofi rose 68% to $2.72 billion. Regeneron had been paying back its share of past development costs out of its Dupixent profits, and that balance was fully repaid at the end of Q2. From Q3 onward, the full profit share flows through, which makes this a lasting step-up rather than a one-time gain.
Dupixent, whose sales Sanofi records, grew 35% to $6.5 billion in the quarter, so the profit pool Regeneron shares in is still expanding.

In the US, EYLEA HD sales jumped 62% to $699 million, while the original EYLEA fell 41% to $400 million. Together, the two brought in about $1.1 billion, down only about 1% from a year earlier, with EYLEA HD now nearly two-thirds of the total. The higher-dose version is now offsetting most of the decline. Libtayo, Regeneron's cancer drug, rose 51% to $550 million.

sum: Sanofi reported strong third-quarter results on Friday, October 30, 2026, and raised its full-year outlook. In its Q3 2026 results press release, the French drugmaker reported sales growth of 14.3% at constant exchange rates and business earnings per share growth of 19.6% on the same basis.

Vaccine sales fell 6.6% to EUR 3.2 billion as respiratory-prevention demand followed its expected phasing. The quarter also included two regulatory approvals, one accepted regulatory submission and two additional designations.

The latest release adds full-quarter net sales of EUR 14.444 billion, IFRS net income of EUR 3.021 billion and free cash flow of EUR 3.269 billion. Business EPS reached EUR 3.55, while IFRS EPS was EUR 2.52; the business figures are non-IFRS measures used by Sanofi to assess operating performance.

Sanofi now expects 2026 sales to grow by a low-teens percentage at constant exchange rates and business EPS to increase by a mid-teens percentage. Why Regeneron (REGN) Stock Is Trading Lower Today
sum: Shares of biotech company Regeneron (NASDAQ:REGN) fell 4% in the afternoon session after the biotechnology company expanded its immunology alliance with Sanofi on terms that left economics for its blockbuster drug Dupixent untouched.

Sanofi will pay Regeneron $1 billion upfront and up to $7 billion in development, regulatory, and commercial milestones for four next-generation, long-acting antibodies, the company said in a press release. The agreement settles prior litigation and calls for both drugmakers to equally split global development costs, commercialization expenses, and future profits, while leaving the existing Dupixent profit-sharing terms unchanged, the company added.The announcement followed investor expectations that a renegotiation might yield better terms on Dupixent, with nearly a quarter of investors surveyed by RBC Capital seeking more constructive economics on the franchise, according to Investing.com. While Sanofi shares rose roughly 2% in European trading, according to Reuters, Regeneron reversed an early morning gain as trading progressed.

By locking in a 50:50 profit split without sweetening Dupixent royalties, Regeneron surrendered half the economics on its next-generation pipeline while committing to co-fund development expenses that Sanofi historically covered upfront. The sell-off reflects a market that viewed the upfront cash as insufficient compensation for diluting long-term margin upside on its most promising immunology follow-ons.
After the initial drop, the shares shed some of the losses and rose to $736.56, down 2.9% from the previous close.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy Regeneron? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

Regeneron's shares are not very volatile and have only had 4 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

items.t: Sanofi Shares Decline as Paul Hudson Removed as CEO, Making Way For Merck KGaA’s Belén Garijo
sum: The sudden departure stands in contrast to other EU pharma leaders who have been given much longer transitions in recent months, including GSK’s Emma Walmsley and Novo Nordisk’s Lars Fruergaard Jørgensen.

Sanofi’s Paul Hudson, who has been heading the venerable pharma’s transition into a modern vaccine company, has been removed from his post after seven years. Merck KGaA’s Belén Garijo will take his place.

Hudson is expected to leave his post at the end of the day on Feb. 17, with Garijo assuming her role at the end of April. For now, Executive VP of General Medicine Olivier Charmeil, will serve as interim CEO.
Sanofi Board Chairman Frédéric Oudéa wished Hudson well in a statement posted Thursday morning.

The swift departure stands in stark contrast to other EU pharma leaders who have been given much longer transitions. GSK’s CEO Emma Walmsley replacement was announced in September last year, but she stayed for three months before stepping aside at the beginning of this year to make way for Luke Miels. She is remaining with the company in a consulting role through September of this year.
Novo Nordisk ousted Lars Fruergaard Jørgensen in May 2025 but left him in charge while it searched for a replacement. Maziar Mike Doustdar ultimately landed the role two months later.
Sanofi’s shares declined 5% to $46.77 in pre-market trading on Thursday morning.

sum: Sanofi sold its controlling stake in the drugmaker's consumer-health unit last year, meaning it's now entirely reliant on innovative prescription medicines.
(Feb 12): Sanofi abruptly replaced chief executive officer Paul Hudson after a massive research spending boost failed to deliver rapid results, appointing Merck KGaA's Belén Garijo to succeed him.

Hudson came under pressure as he tried to replace sales from a looming patent cliff for its top-selling asthma and skin disease drug Dupixent. The efforts didn't succeed after a little over six years at the helm, with three key late-stage trials showing mixed or negative results last year.
"Investors remain frustrated with the repeated R&D (research and development) failures," said Abhishek Raval, an analyst at AlphaValue.
Sanofi shares fell as much as 1.2% in early Paris trading on Thursday. The stock has declined 21% over the past 12 months.

Garijo's term at Merck was ending soon and the Spanish executive knows Sanofi well, having spent 15 years there. She will "bring an increased rigor to the implementation of Sanofi's strategy", the drugmaker said in a statement. Her priority will be to strengthen the productivity, governance, and innovation capacity of R&D, it added.

Hudson set out an ambitious plan meant to turbo-charge new drugs to market in 2023. That strategy has not yet delivered results. In 2024 an experimental multiple sclerosis drug tolebrutinib failed a late-stage trial in a form of multiple sclerosis, and US regulators rejected it in another indication. Another experimental medicine for atopic dermatitis called amlitelimab — which investors had hoped could succeed Dupixent — has seen mixed results in trials.
